title: The Signal (Garshin) -- The Signalman's Dangerous Decision

source_brief: This is Vsevolod Garshin's 1887 short story "The Signal" (Russian: Сигнал), in an early-1900s English translation by Lizzie B. Gorin, sourced from a Project Gutenberg public-domain anthology of Russian short stories ("Told by the Colonists: The Best Russian Short Stories"). Semen Ivanov, a sickly ex-soldier, works as a railway trackman with his wife at a remote watch-house. His only neighbor, fellow trackman Vasili, grows increasingly bitter about unfair treatment by railway officials: low pay, petty punishments over small things like an unreported vegetable patch, and finally being struck in the face by an inspecting officer after a minor complaint. Vasili leaves to seek justice through official channels in the city and comes back changed, worn down, and desperate. Later, while out gathering wood, Semen discovers Vasili on the tracks prying a rail loose with a crowbar -- an act of sabotage and revenge -- just before a passenger train full of people, including children, is due. Unable to talk Vasili out of it, fix the rail with his bare hands, or reach his watch-house and back in time to fetch a warning flag, Semen improvises: he cuts his own arm with his knife and waves a handkerchief soaked in his blood as an emergency red danger signal to warn the oncoming train in time.
